Principles

Foundation
Clear first

Reduce effort to understand

Hierarchy and language should help recruiters find the project, role, decision, and outcome quickly.

Craft with purpose

Color, glass, and motion add character while keeping the work and its reasoning at the center.

Curiosity in layers

Reward closer attention

04a

Home Hero

Review

hero-portrait · Approved artwork
Transparent charcoal SVG. Preserve the glass card’s labels and tilt. Header displays Alfie Liu; Dock provides Work, About, and Resume.

Headline and status dot

The headline and introduction stream in once. The headline then cycles complex, financial, and AI-powered every 3.6 seconds while “easier to use” keeps a one-time green highlight. The status dot pulses while the Hero is visible.

Offscreen and background motion pauses. Reduced-motion mode shows “Making complex products easier to use” without the word cycle or pulse.

Navigation

Experimental

Bottom Dock

Translucent glass · Active · Hover · Focus · Always visible

Light floating navigation keeps Work, About, and Resume available while scrolling. The translucent surface retains a solid fallback, and each item has a 44px touch target. Resume opens the supplied PDF in a new tab.

WorkAboutResume

Case Navigation

Desktop sidebar · Glass progress · Previous / Next cycle

Wide screens use a persistent Back link and contents list. Narrower screens show a return link above the title. Every case ends with a Previous work / Next project pair: regular-weight muted labels and dark project names, cycling through all four projects and stacking below 900px. The Dock’s Work item is not marked active on case pages.

Site footer

Desktop row · Stacked mobile · Hover · Focus

Shared across public pages. The location reads Vancouver; the full email address remains a mailto link that can also be copied. Text underlines appear close to the letters only on hover or keyboard focus. Primary links keep 44px touch targets and a visible focus outline.

06a

About gallery

Review

Personal photo gallery

Staggered · Overflowing pointer caption · Focus · Touch · Reduced motion

Three complete photos form a quiet, uneven vertical rhythm. Fine pointers show a light-glass label that can cross the photo edge but stays inside the viewport; keyboard focus, touch, and reduced motion keep it fixed and visible.

07

Project cards

Review

Primary project card

Transparent editorial row · Split desktop · Stacked mobile

Use for the two strongest case studies. Real imagery carries the color; the row has no filled card surface, and verified highlights are optional. Hover or keyboard focus turns only the title green, while the image zooms 2.5% inside its frame and the CTA arrow shifts slightly; no title underline.

Secondary project cards

16:9 media · Shared top rule · Two-column desktop · Single-column mobile

Use for shorter stories without numeric ordering, metadata blocks, or unverified highlights. The shorter 16:9 media keeps the pair visually subordinate; both cards share one continuous divider on desktop and use the same restrained image zoom as the primary cards.

09

Usage rules

Foundation
1. Discuss by component and state.

Example: “Primary project card / split / hover” instead of “the large box on the homepage.”

2. Change tokens before isolated values.

Global color, spacing, radius, type, and motion changes belong in shared tokens.

3. Test here, then check real pages.

The component page reveals consistency; the portfolio confirms that the rule works with real content.

4. Record exceptions.

If a project needs a unique pattern, document why it cannot use an existing variant.

5. Mark maturity.

Stable is safe to reuse. Review needs a decision. Experimental can change after prototype feedback.
